steps.body: Rounding is perfect for quick real-world estimates — but WHEN you round matters. You can round each number first, then add (fast). Or you can add the exact numbers first, then round the total (more precise). These two paths don't always agree.

numericErrors.feedback: 87,100 is the EXACT sum before rounding. This step just adds the already-rounded pieces: 60,000 + 20,000 = 80,000.
20,000 is only one of the two rounded pieces. Add both: 60,000 + 20,000 = 80,000.

steps.body: Notice: those two paths gave **different answers** — 80,000 versus 90,000. Rounding each number first can drift away from the truly rounded total, especially when the pieces are each close to rolling over. **For an accurate rounded estimate, always add exact numbers first, then round once.**

explanationVariants: Adding the exact numbers first, then rounding the total once, gives the TRUE rounded sum.
Rounding each piece before adding can drift from the real rounded total.
